source.verification_notes: This record's retained evidence is extracted from Apple's general 'Identify your iPod model' page, not an individual technical-specifications page. The archived HTML file is the shared source page. Only identification facts explicitly present in that page are supported; detailed technical specifications require separate model-specific sources.
notes: Primary evidence is Apple's official iPod identification page; it supports only the model-identification statements retained in the source section.

Do not treat this source as a complete technical specification sheet. Model-specific Apple technical-specification pages have been discovered for some models and remain to be archived and mapped individually.

Model-specific Apple technical-specification source preserved section-by-section from https://support.apple.com/en-ie/112507 (apple_remaining_extraction/technical_specs_html/ipod-nano-1st-generation-tech-specs.html); First-generation iPod nano technical specifications; model/capacity identity remains separately sourced from Apple's identification page. Typed normalized values were not inferred by this archival pass.

sections.heading: iPod nano
sections.source_text:
Navigation: Click Wheel
Capacity: 1, 2 and 4 GB
Model numbers and dates introduced: A1137: February 2006 A1137: September 2005
Model numbers and dates introduced:
A1137: February 2006
A1137: September 2005
iPod nano is smaller than iPod mini and has a colour screen and a Click Wheel, but has flash memory instead of a hard drive. You sync music and photos with a USB 2 cable – not FireWire. The capacity of the iPod nano is engraved on the back of the case.
iPod nano comes in white and black.

sections.heading: Capacity
sections.source_text:
1GB, 2GB or 4GB flash drive

sections.heading: Display
sections.source_text:
1.5 inch (diagonal) liquid crystal display with blue-white LED backlight
176 x 132 pixel resolution, .168-mm dot pitch
Support for display of multiple languages and characters simultaneously

sections.heading: Audio
sections.source_text:
Skip-free playback
Frequency response: 20Hz to 20,000Hz
Audio formats supported: AAC (16 to 320 Kbps), Protected AAC (from iTunes Music Store), MP3 (16 to 320 Kbps), MP3 VBR, Audible (formats 2, 3 and 4), Apple Lossless, AIFF and WAV
Upgradable firmware enables support for future audio formats

sections.heading: Headphones
sections.source_text:
Earbud-style headphones with 18-mm drivers using Neodymium transducer magnets
Frequency response: 20Hz to 20,000Hz
Impedance: 32 ohms

sections.heading: Mac system requirements
sections.source_text:
Macintosh computer with USB port (USB 2.0 recommended)
Mac OS X v10.3.4 or later

sections.heading: Windows system requirements
sections.source_text:
PC with USB port or card (USB 2.0 recommended)
Windows 2000 with Service Pack 4 or later, or Windows XP Home or Professional with Service Pack 2 or later

sections.heading: Environmental requirements
sections.source_text:
Operating temperature: 32° to 95° F (0° to 35° C)
Non operating temperature: -4° to 113° F (-20° to 45° C)
Relative humidity: 5% to 95% noncondensing
Maximum operating altitude: 10,000 feet (3000 m)
